builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs
summary: LOWN replaces the default DVLM decoding loop that reprocesses all visual tokens at every denoising step with a certificate mechanism: it predicts masked tokens without the image and only runs an image-conditioned pass when predictions disagree, reusing the certified earlier prediction otherwise. It costs no training and adds modest complexity (an extra text-only forward pass per step and disagreement bookkeeping), and it composes with visual token pruning and KV caching, but it only applies to LLaDA-family diffusion VLMs, not to the autoregressive VLMs that dominate production deployments. It can fail on workloads where image dependence is high or non-stationary, since the measured 22.8% disagreement rate varies across benchmarks and accuracy retention is demonstrated only on the ten reported benchmarks.
rationale: The method is training-free, open-source, and single-GPU compatible with a substantial FLOP reduction, but its value is confined to teams actually deploying LLaDA-based diffusion VLMs, so adoption must be validated against that specific model family and workload.
technique: Certificate-guided adaptive visual routing for DVLMs

claims.statement: LOWN replaces the default DVLM decoding loop that reprocesses all visual tokens at every denoising step with a certificate mechanism: it predicts masked tokens without the image and only runs an image-conditioned pass when predictions disagree, reusing the certified earlier prediction otherwise. It costs no training and adds modest complexity (an extra text-only forward pass per step and disagreement bookkeeping), and it composes with visual token pruning and KV caching, but it only applies to LLaDA-family diffusion VLMs, not to the autoregressive VLMs that dominate production deployments. It can fail on workloads where image dependence is high or non-stationary, since the measured 22.8% disagreement rate varies across benchmarks and accuracy retention is demonstrated only on the ten reported benchmarks.
Retains 99.6% of LLaDA-V's score on ten benchmarks at 35.3% of the decoding FLOPs on average (roughly 2.8x FLOP reduction), without training or a tuned threshold.
